title: Comparison with the Stacks Project adic constructible category
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, and let
$\operatorname{Res}\colon D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_{E,X})\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},(\cO_E)_X)$ be restriction
of scalars along the map from the constant sheaf. Let $\Dc(X,\cO_E)$ be the full subcategory of
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},(\cO_E)_X)$ of \stacks{09C1}: derived $\pi_E$-complete complexes $L$ such that
$L\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_E}\cO_E/\pi_E$ has finite Tor dimension and constructible cohomology
sheaves (pulled back from $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$). Then for $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_{E,X})$:
$$
K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)\iff\operatorname{Res}K\in\Dc(X,\cO_E),
$$
and $\operatorname{Res}$ restricts to an equivalence $\Dbc(X,\cO_E)\simeq\Dc(X,\cO_E)$.

proof.text:
Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, $k=R/\pi_E$, and $L=\operatorname{Res}K$. The coefficient map is $c:R_X\to B$. The completed coefficient identification in [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] and parts (1), (3) of [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients] identify $B/\pi_E^n$ with $(R/\pi_E^n)_X$ and give, for every $n\geq1$, a canonical isomorphism
$$L\otimes_{R_X}^{\mathbf L}(R/\pi_E^n)_X\simeq K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}(R/\pi_E^n)_X.$$
In particular the first reduction on the two sides is one and the same object $M$ of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},k_X)$. This uses derived relative tensor products, not an ordinary quotient of the cohomology sheaves.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-local-completeness] to $c:R_X\to B$ and to the ideal subsheaf $(\pi_E)\subset R_X$. Its extended ideal is $(\pi_E)B$. Thus $K$ is derived $(\pi_E)B$-complete if and only if $L$ is derived $(\pi_E)$-complete. This applies to the arbitrary complex $K$ in the statement: it is not inferred merely from an equivalence already restricted to complete objects. To relate this local definition to the quotient-tower completeness used in [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients], apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] with $A=R$ and $I=(\pi_E)$. The ring $R$ is a discrete valuation ring by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]; every ideal is principal, hence finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian. The ideal $I$ has the single generator $\pi_E$, and $B$ is precisely its completed constant sheaf by step 1. The last paragraph of that theorem identifies the local completeness condition with the quotient-tower completion unit for both $R_X$ and $B$. Thus the same equivalence of completeness conditions holds with either convention; in particular it applies to the complete subcategories used in step 5.

proof.text:
The residue ring $k$ is a finite discrete field [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], hence Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$). Choose a finite affine cover of $X$ by spectra of Noetherian rings. Each member has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. An increasing chain of opens of $X$ stabilizes on each cover member and hence, taking the maximum of finitely many stabilization indices, on $X$. Thus every open of $X$ is quasi-compact: the finite unions of any open covering have a maximal member by the ascending-chain condition, and that member must contain every covering open. In particular $X$ is quasi-compact and intersections of two affine opens are quasi-compact, so $X$ is quasi-separated. For any $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},k_X)$, finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ implies $H^i(M)=0$ off $[a,b]$ by taking the tensor test module to be $k_X$, the unit of the derived tensor structure [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Consequently [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] and [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] give the equivalence of the following conditions: $M$ has constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude; and $M\simeq\nu_X^*C$ for a bounded constructible étale $k$-complex $C$ of finite Tor amplitude. The first cited comparison supplies the bounded étale object, and the second preserves and reflects its Tor interval; it is not enough to cite only a definition of flatness or only a sheaf comparison.

The local finite Tor condition in the Stacks definition gives the same category here. Choose a pro-étale covering on which Tor intervals exist. By the covering condition of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and a finite affine cover of the Noetherian $X$, finitely many affine pieces of that covering still cover $X$. Take the minimum of their lower bounds and the maximum of their upper bounds. The cohomology sheaves of $M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N$ vanish off this interval after restriction to every piece, for every $N$, and hence vanish, since a sheaf zero on a covering is zero. To make the locality argument explicit, use a resolution with K-flat flat terms from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Slice restriction is exact [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction] and is sectionwise restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], so it commutes with the ordinary tensor of representative complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] the restricted resolution still computes the derived tensor. Thus both cohomology and the tensor calculation used to test a Tor bound agree with their restrictions.

For the reverse local implication, assume the global Tor bound and constructible cohomology of $M$. The comparison just proved gives $C\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},k)$ with the same Tor interval $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] to this $C$: its hypotheses hold because $k$ is finite and $X$ is Noetherian. Obtain a termwise flat complex $P$ representing $C$, zero outside $[a,b]$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Pulling $P$ back along the geometric morphism $\nu_X$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] computes $\nu_X^*C\simeq M$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] makes the resulting complex termwise flat and K-flat. Apply that same lemma to each slice restriction. For an arbitrary module sheaf $N$ on the slice, its derived tensor with this restricted complex is therefore represented by the ordinary tensor with $N[0]$, whose terms are zero outside $[a,b]$. Thus every slice has the bound $[a,b]$, including test modules that do not come by restriction from $X$. When $X$ is empty all module sheaves are zero and one may take $[a,b]=[0,0]$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-integral-cohomological-adic-criterion], the bounded constructible cohomology condition $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is equivalent to derived completeness of $K$ together with the condition that its first reduction $M$ is $\nu_X^*C$ for an étale bounded constructible complex $C$ of finite Tor amplitude. Steps 1 and 2 replace these respectively by the first reduction and derived completeness of $L$, and step 3 replaces the residue condition by constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude of $L\otimes_{R_X}^{\mathbf L}k_X$. These are exactly the two defining conditions for $L\in\Dc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. This proves both implications without assuming at the outset that $K$ is complete.

proof.text: Part (2) of [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients] makes $\operatorname{Res}$ an equivalence between the full subcategories of derived complete complexes. By step 4 the selected bounded constructible objects correspond precisely under this equivalence. Its restriction is fully faithful because its Hom maps are unchanged. For essential surjectivity, take $L\in\Dc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and a derived complete preimage $K$ supplied by that equivalence; step 4 then gives $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Thus restriction of scalars gives the claimed equivalence of full subcategories.
